title: The Hidden Ocean
narration: Beneath a cracked shell of ice, there's an ocean with twice the water of all Earth's seas combined. Could something be swimming in it? This moon, just 3,100 kilometers across, might cradle secrets.
visual_goal: Close-up of Europa's icy surface cracking, revealing a dark ocean below

title: Galileo's Discovery
narration: In January 1610, Galileo Galilei spotted a tiny dot orbiting Jupiter. He had no idea it held an ocean. That pinprick of light changed our cosmic perspective forever.
visual_goal: Old telescope view of Jupiter and its moons, then Galileo's sketch

title: The Icy Shell
narration: Europa's surface is mostly water ice, reflecting 67% of sunlight. Temperature: minus 160 degrees Celsius. That brilliant white shell hides a dark, liquid heart beneath.
visual_goal: Bright icy surface with cracks, reflecting sunlight

title: Tidal Lock
narration: Europa is gravitationally locked with Jupiter. One side always faces the giant planet. That constant pull squeezes its insides, generating heat that keeps the hidden ocean liquid.
visual_goal: Europa orbiting Jupiter, always showing same face, with tidal bulges

title: The Magnetic Clue
narration: In the late 1990s, the Galileo spacecraft measured Europa's magnetic field. The data hinted at something conductive beneath the ice—a fingerprint of saline water moving with the tides.
visual_goal: Spacecraft measuring magnetic field lines around Europa

title: Ocean's Depth
narration: That ocean runs 60 to 150 kilometers below the ice—over ten times the depth of Earth's Mariana Trench. An abyss that dwarfs anything on our planet.
visual_goal: Cross-section of Europa showing thick ice and deep ocean

title: Juno's Flyby
narration: In 2022, NASA's Juno spacecraft flew within 352 kilometers of Europa—closer than the ISS is to Earth. The moon's fractured face filled the entire view, revealing chaos and promise.
visual_goal: Juno spacecraft flying past Europa, surface details rushing by

title: A Day on Europa
narration: A day on Europa lasts 3.55 Earth days. Each slow rotation offers a new angle on the same eternal mystery.
visual_goal: Time-lapse of Europa rotating against starfield

title: The Clipper Arrives
narration: The Europa Clipper launched in 2024, arriving in 2030 to study that ocean—looking for signs of habitability. Dozens of flybys will peel back layers of the enigma.
visual_goal: Europa Clipper spacecraft flying over Europa's surface with instruments

title: The Final Question
narration: Could something live in that alien ocean? Scientists think Europa is one of the most promising places. The answer might redefine our place in the universe—if we dare to search.
visual_goal: Europa's ocean with hypothetical life forms, then question mark fading in
